method: Single-evaluator cognitive walkthrough using hypothetical user perspectives and recorded UI actions. These are test scenarios, not research-validated customer personas or independent participants.
target: Latest Windows development build and Android companion
guardrails: Use disposable profiles, projects and synthetic results.
Do not submit paid AI work, install agents, expose credentials, contact users or change production data.
Record actual UI behavior separately from predicted confusion or desired features.
Do not report adoption rates, willingness to pay, fictional customer quotes or participant success percentages.

assumptions: Has not used an agent CLI
Has a folder they want help with
scenarios.task: Explain what Paddock does, identify the account/software requirements and start one useful conversation in the chosen folder.
scenarios.real_user_question: Without using the guide, show where you would begin and explain what you expect the next screen to do.

scenarios.perspective: Existing CLI user working on several projects
assumptions: Already knows Claude Code or Codex
Wants to resume the correct work without losing context
scenarios.task: Open and distinguish two consoles, associate an existing folder with a project, and find the files from an older completed prompt.
checkpoints: Existing projects do not require unnecessary setup
scenarios.real_user_question: Use your existing repository. What would make you switch from your current terminal setup?

scenarios.perspective: PC user checking work from an Android phone
assumptions: Has a Windows PC running Paddock
Wants to read an answer, reply and handle a permission request
May be unfamiliar with router configuration
scenarios.task: Pair the phone, identify the active PC/chat, send a message, answer a folder prompt and find the completed result.
checkpoints: Connection failure has a recovery path
scenarios.real_user_question: Show how you would reply to this console. What do you expect to work when you leave your Wi-Fi?

scenarios.perspective: User evaluating access, privacy and provider costs
assumptions: Wants to understand local storage, phone access and billable requests
Does not want optional tools configured automatically
scenarios.task: Distinguish subscription access from API billing, inspect where keys/tools are configured, understand phone access and find removal/update controls.
checkpoints: Provider account versus API key is clear
Usage is distinguished from estimated spending
Removal and update consequences are explained
scenarios.real_user_question: Explain which actions could cost money and which computer/files the phone can access. Show where you would check your answer.
